clue.text: The rest of the workers call for help

definitions.meaning: ..., 1 May, is the traditional workers' holiday, a day of rest for labour
the international radio distress signal used by ships and aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the rest of the workforce are shouting for help about.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one sentence the clue seems to describe workers calling out; split after 'workers' it gives two separate senses of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase for the workers' holiday is also the spoken distress signal of radio operators.

clue.text: Centre of a dance revolution

parts.note: read not as a political uprising but as the pole at the middle of a spring dance where ribboned dancers literally revolve around it

explanation.surface: Something sounds like the heart of a political uprising in the dance world.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring-festival pole stands in the middle while dancers circle it with ribbons, so it is literally the centre of their revolving.

clue.text: Submit a return

definitions.meaning: to give way or surrender to pressure
the profit or output produced by an investment or crop

explanation.surface: A form-filler is told to hand in a tax return.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to give way and the amount produced, like a crop's output or an investment's profit.

clue.text: Roman general has a hold on father

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of another comes first

parts.note: a grip is a firm hold
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A Roman commander keeps his father firmly under control.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one piece written 'on' another sits above it, so the order is kept top to bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Agrippa was the Roman general and admiral who won at Actium for Augustus.

clue.text: Head dancer?

parts.note: not a principal ballerina but the biblical dancer who was rewarded with John the Baptist's head on a platter

explanation.surface: Who leads the dance troupe?
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel story Herod's stepdaughter danced for him and asked for the Baptist's head as her reward.

clue.text: The overflowing craft of poetry

parts.note: read not as a poet's prolific skill but as a richly laden merchant ship, a literary and poetic word for such a vessel

explanation.surface: A poet's abundant skill at writing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a large merchant vessel loaded with riches, used chiefly in poetry and literature.

clue.text: Start to make a speech without a single drink

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside: the speech word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a formal speech
I is the Roman numeral one
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone begins a speech without taking a single drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense it means outside, so the speech word goes round the others.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or start something off; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Got together after an important point cropped up

indicators.note: the merging word comes after the point letter

parts.note: E, east, is one of the cardinal points of the compass
merged means joined together

explanation.surface: People met up once a crucial point had arisen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Important point' is a cardinal compass point, here E for east.
explanation.definitionFit: To emerge is to come into view or appear, just as something that has cropped up has arisen.

clue.text: National emblem put down on the list going out

parts.note: to scotch a rumour or plan is to put a stop to it

indicators.note: the words are thrown out of order, suggesting a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A national symbol is struck off the list and leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' just joins the two halves; 'going out' rearranges THE LIST into THISTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The prickly purple wild plant of Scotland is that country's national floral symbol.

clue.text: Use the office keys?

parts.note: not unlocking a door but pressing the letter keys of a keyboard at work to produce text

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to use the keys to unlock the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the keys of a typewriter or keyboard to produce text is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Showed appreciation for creation of co-designer

indicators.note: what is created from the letters is a new arrangement of them

explanation.surface: Someone thanked a fellow designer for their creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Creation of' reworks the letters of CO-DESIGNER.
explanation.definitionFit: To recognise someone's work is to acknowledge and show appreciation for it.

clue.text: Support by arms or threaten by them

definitions.meaning: to hold something up is to support it with one's arms
here 'arms' means weapons: a robbery at gunpoint is a stick-up

explanation.surface: Arms can be used to prop something up or to menace somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms' shifts from limbs in the first half to weapons in the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to lift and support, and also to rob with weapons as in a stick-up.

clue.text: Oral examinations for wine buyers?

parts.note: not spoken exams but sampling wine by mouth before purchase

explanation.surface: Wine merchants apparently have to sit spoken tests.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine buyers sample by mouth, so their oral examinations are sessions where wines are sipped and judged.

clue.text: Misery of a teacher working with horrible head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
working suggests the letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher is miserable working under a horrible headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible head' is the H of horrible; 'working' rearranges A TEACHER to EARTACHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartache is emotional anguish or grief, so it is a synonym of misery.

clue.text: Surplus to requirements and turned off

indicators.note: off as in gone off or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A worker is told they are no longer needed and is switched off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned off' reads as a second definition, but 'off' rearranges AND TURNED, and 'turned' is fodder, not a meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something no longer needed is superfluous, the exact sense of the adjective, used too of laid-off workers.

clue.text: Property to come down

definitions.meaning: real estate, ground owned by someone
to alight or touch down after flying

explanation.surface: Property prices are about to fall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ground owned as an estate, and as a verb to come down to earth as a plane does.

clue.text: Fools the youngsters

definitions.meaning: teases or deceives, as in 'you're joking me'

explanation.surface: The young ones play the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to tease or hoodwink; as a plural noun it means children.

clue.text: A professor of infinite wisdom

parts.note: not an academic but someone who professes, or claims, to know everything

explanation.surface: An academic whose wisdom has no limits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Professor' is one who professes, i.e. claims, not a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: The term mocks a person who claims to have all the answers, professing boundless knowledge.

clue.text: Horror of man beset by terrible spectre

indicators.note: the man is surrounded on all sides by the other letters
something terrible is messed up, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A man is plagued by a frightful ghost and is horrified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges the ghost word to TCREEPS, and 'beset by' surrounds the man with it, his two letters going in after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a feeling of fear or revulsion, an informal word for a sense of horror.

clue.text: Second man fitting in as chief officer

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Cain, the first son of Adam, was the second man in the Bible's story
apt means fitting or suitable

explanation.surface: A deputy fits in well as the chief officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second man' looks like a deputy but is the Biblical Cain, born after Adam.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's commanding officer, or the leader of a team, is its chief.

clue.text: Artist keeps a boat by the bank

definitions.meaning: one who makes pictures with paint

definitions.text: keeps a boat by the bank
definitions.meaning: a rope at a boat's bow used to tie it up to a bank or quay

explanation.surface: An artist keeps a boat moored next to the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names someone who paints and also the bow rope that ties a small boat to a mooring.

clue.text: Wrongly arrest French intellectual

indicators.note: the letters are set out wrongly, i.e. in a new order

explanation.surface: A French thinker is wrongfully detained.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was the French existentialist philosopher and writer, a leading intellectual.

clue.text: Legislation that went against the grain

definitions.text: Legislation that went against the grain

parts.words: Legislation that went against the grain
parts.note: not laws that were unpopular but statutes about grain itself, restricting cereal imports in nineteenth-century Britain

explanation.surface: Some unpopular legislation that people resented.
explanation.walkthrough: These were British tariffs on imported cereal, repealed in 1846.
explanation.definitionFit: The British statutes restricting cereal imports literally legislated about grain, and were widely resented.

clue.text: Its lead decreases and it often draws

definitions.text: Its lead decreases and it often draws

parts.words: Its lead decreases and it often draws
parts.note: sounds like a sports team losing its lead and drawing matches, but describes a writing tool whose graphite wears down as it sketches

explanation.surface: A football team keeps losing its lead and drawing games.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden drawing implement has a graphite core, called lead, that wears down with use.

clue.text: Innocent one in church body

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An innocent person sits in the main part of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naive means lacking experience or guile, which is a sense of innocent.

clue.text: Dance with Jack before everyone retires

parts.note: a jack tar is a sailor, so Jack gives TAR
ante is Latin for before

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A sailor dances before everyone goes to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantella is a fast whirling Italian folk dance.

clue.text: I turn to a matter of trivial importance

indicators.note: turning round the short word means reading it backwards

explanation.surface: Someone turns to something of no importance.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' of the surface is just the letter itself, and 'turn' acts only on the little word next to it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek letter is used to mean a very small amount, a jot or a whit.

clue.text: Vehicle it is illegal to leave in the street

definitions.meaning: a curtained couch carried on poles, an old conveyance

definitions.text: it is illegal to leave in the street
definitions.meaning: rubbish dropped in public, an offence

explanation.surface: Someone notes that leaving a car in the street is against the law.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests illegal parking; the vehicle is an old carried couch, and the second sense is rubbish dropped in public.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a carried bed used as transport, and also rubbish discarded in public places.

clue.text: Create goodwill by being a close listener

parts.note: close as a noun is an end or conclusion
the ear is the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A good listener nearby wins people's affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is the noun meaning end, not the adjective meaning near.
explanation.definitionFit: To endear is to win affection or favour, which creates goodwill.
